why: Sort by a tuple key: count each value's frequency, then sort the items by (frequency, value), so the primary order is frequency and ties fall back to the value itself.
hints: You need two things per item: its frequency and its value. Where does the frequency come from?
Count with a hash map first. Then the order you want is 'by frequency, then by value': a two-part key.
sorted(items, key=lambda x: (freq[x], x)). Every copy of a value has the same key, so copies stay together. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Return all copies, not just the distinct values.
Ties on frequency are broken by the smaller value, not by first appearance.
